title: Direct Lean 4 proof of FFLLW chromatic number bound from Mathlib primitives

problemStatement.formal: For finite G, prove G.chromaticNumber < G.egirth -> admitsRobustAcyclicOrientation G; in the rank-based formulation this follows from the stronger coloring-orientation result.
problemStatement.plain: A direct Lean 4 proof of the Fisher-Fraughnaugh-Langley-West (FFLLW) theorem from Mathlib primitives: if χ(G) < girth(G), then G admits a robustly acyclic orientation. The proof constructs the coloring orientation (orient u→v when col(u) < col(v)) and shows it is always robustly acyclic. Key insight: under the rank-based formulation, ANY properly colorable finite graph has a robust orientation, making the girth condition unnecessary.
whyMatters: It explains why the rank-based Erdos1006 formalization makes FFLLW immediate from colorability.

proven: `coloringOrientation_robustlyAcyclic` proves the coloring orientation is rank-based robustly acyclic.
`ffllw_direct` proves the FFLLW implication as a corollary.
`every_finite_graph_has_robust` proves every finite graph has a rank-based robust orientation.
open: Classical path-based robustness remains a separate question from the rank-based result.
